extracted.intended_audience: general newspaper readers interested in wartime events (Belgium/Netherlands/UK/France)
extracted.subtask_description: A contemporaneous newspaper dispatch reporting military operations, air raids, casualties, government actions, and public reactions during an invasion in Western Europe. Emphasizes official communiqués, eyewitness details, and shifting/unconfirmed reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite official communiqués and government statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Use official communiques and government announcements as primary sourcing (e.g., "A late-day communique said the Belgians are continuing their fight...", "The radio announced this afternoon that Queen Wilhelmina had sent a message...").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Naming and quoting official communiques provides authoritative information on military positions, casualty counts, and government actions; indicate the issuing body and date/time. Where available, include direct quotes and attributions (e.g., Dutch Foreign Minister Van Kleffens, Belgian Defense Minister Gen. Henri Denis).

rubrics_metrics.name: Flag unconfirmed versus confirmed reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Make clear which items are verified and which are "unconfirmed" or "reported" (e.g., "Unconfirmed advices that German forces in Belgium had reached the outer defenses of Liege...").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Label claims that are not independently verifiable; use phrases like 'unconfirmed advices,' 'reported,' or 'a British broadcast said' to avoid presenting speculation as fact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report contradictory or competing accounts
rubrics_metrics.description: When sources disagree, present the conflicting accounts (e.g., German claims vs. Allied/British denials: "The British denied any such Allied raid, but said they bombed German troops back of the western front.").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly show differing perspectives (Allied, German, neutral agencies) and avoid resolving disputes unless corroborated. Note the source for each version.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide casualty and damage figures with sourcing
rubrics_metrics.description: Give counts of dead, injured, and material damage and attribute them (e.g., "at least fifty persons... forty-one dead and eighty-two injured", "The Netherlands reported taking a toll of more than 100 German planes").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report numbers but attribute to the reporting agency or government and indicate if figures are estimates or provisional.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe exact times and alarm cycles for air raids
rubrics_metrics.description: Include specific times and sequence of alarms (e.g., "This morning’s first alarm sounded at 6:15 A.M... the second fifty-five minutes later.").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timing of raids and alarms helps convey tempo and public response; when possible provide local and reference-zone times.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include geographic detail and distances
rubrics_metrics.description: Give place names and distances to situate events (e.g., "Namur, thirty-five miles southeast of the capital", "Dinant, fifteen miles south of Namur").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use recognizable geographic references and distances to help readers understand locations and front lines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish types of military actions (parachute drops, air raids, ground advances)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify the mode of attack and tactical details (e.g., "German parachute troops had landed...", "smashing German aerial troop transports into junk").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe whether engagements involve airborne insertions, bombing raids, ground assaults, coastal landings, or sabotage (fifth column) to clarify the operational picture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report on civil defense and public measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Cover civilian responses and protections (e.g., blackouts, rationing, evacuations: "Food rationing at fixed prices started today... blackout... slung on their gas mask containers").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include information about blackouts, rationing, evacuations, shelters and government orders to convey societal impact and preparedness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use eyewitness and correspondent detail for immediacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Incorporate on-scene observations (e.g., correspondent watching from the Associated Press bureau: "The bombs hit about 200 yards from the window from which this correspondent was watching").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: First-hand descriptions add immediacy; identify whether the account is from a staff correspondent, wire service, or local source.

rubrics_metrics.name: Note censorship and information control
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledge government censorship or restricted reporting (e.g., "the Government kept strict censor-...", references to cut-off radio programs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When censorship or information blackout is in effect, report its presence and how it may limit or shape available information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attribute operational claims to named agencies (news agencies, ministries, radio)
rubrics_metrics.description: Attribute major claims to their originating news or government agency (e.g., DNB, Reuters, Associated Press, British Air Ministry, Dutch radio).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Naming the agency increases source transparency and lets readers assess potential biases or reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report diplomatic and political reaction alongside military events
rubrics_metrics.description: Include governmental and royal statements and political developments (e.g., Churchill replacing Chamberlain, Queen Wilhelmina's appeal to King of Italy, King George VI's messages of sympathy).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contextualize battlefield developments with high-level political/diplomatic responses that affect public morale and policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantify and contextualize air/ground losses with care
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide aggregate tallies and opposing claims while noting possible inflation or propaganda (e.g., "the Allies said they had shot down, captured or damaged at least 180 German planes... the Germans declared 100 Allied planes were destroyed").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present both sides' loss claims and flag them as mutually conflicting; indicate that such figures may be propaganda or provisional.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report on fifth-column/fear-of-collaboration incidents
rubrics_metrics.description: Cover reports of internal sabotage or collaboration (e.g., attempts to seize police HQ, German residents bearing orders, arrests of Rexist leader Leon Degrelle).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document arrests, identified collaborators, and government countermeasures; distinguish rumor from substantiated arrests or found documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include logistical and strategic details (fortifications, inundation, bridges blown)
rubrics_metrics.description: Mention defensive measures and terrain effects (e.g., Netherlands defense by flooded lowlands, blown bridges on the Nieuwe Maas, German West Wall fortifications).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how terrain and engineered defenses influence operations; report known construction or counter-construction (e.g., orders to build new fortifications).
